raw_response:
I've been growing cotton on this same land for decades. Quzhou is cotton country — my father grew it, I grew it, and this year is no different. I have 10.1 mu, well water, and I know what works here.

I'll plant all 10.1 mu in cotton, same as every year. No reason to change. I'll buy the hybrid Bt cotton seeds from the township supply co-op — the kind with bollworm resistance built in. I've used improved hybrids for years now; the old traditional varieties can't compete anymore.

Before planting in late April, I'll plough the field deep. I've always ploughed. My neighbor tried no-till once and had problems with weeds and compaction. I know how to plough, and the soil here responds well to it.

For fertilizer, I'll put down base fertilizer before planting — phosphorus and potassium go in the ground at the start. Then I'll top-dress with nitrogen twice: once when the plants are knee-high, and again at flowering. The well water helps me time the top-dressing right after irrigation so the roots take it up. Total nitrogen I use is around 18 kg per mu. Phosphorus about 10, potassium about 8. That's what I've settled on over the years.

Irrigation: I'll water before planting to get good germination, then at squaring, at peak flowering, and once more at boll-setting if August is dry. Four times usually does it.

Pesticides — cotton needs watching. Aphids in June, spider mites in the heat of July, and I still check for bollworm even with Bt seed. I'll spray about 7 times through the season. Can't let pests get ahead of you.

If the weather is decent, I expect around 300 kg per mu of seed cotton. Had 310 last year. 300 is honest.
